summary: A deploy that recreates nora, presence and analytics from one image at the same time no longer crashes one of them with a duplicate-column migration error.
details: `run_migrations` and `stamp_head` now serialize behind a Postgres session-level advisory lock before running Alembic: a losing process waits, then finds the database already at head and does nothing, instead of racing another process's `ALTER TABLE`.

Observed live 2026-09-24 deploying migration 0062: presence lost the race, raised `psycopg.errors.DuplicateColumn`, and crashed before its one restart came up clean. A single process's startup is unaffected — acquire, migrate, release is the same shape it already ran.
limitations: Only guards this repo's own `run_migrations`/`stamp_head` callers; an operator running raw `alembic` from the CLI against a live database is not covered.
